all_findings.description:
FIND — scan_health() misreports missing tools as available. In bench/endocrine.py, each runner returns `[]` when `_run_tool()` reports `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`, and scan_health() then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` unconditionally unless an exception was raised. Evidence: run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy all convert NOT_FOUND into empty diagnostics instead of surfacing unavailability, and scan_health has no other availability check.
FOLLOW: This creates a fail-open health scan: the endocrine layer can report a clean scan with zero diagnostics while all analyzers are absent. insect_brain consumes health_scan as a structured health signal for round decisions; zero diagnostics from “available” tools is materially different from “tool unavailable”. It also corrupts reviewer-facing telemetry and can hide infrastructure regressions in the PoC happy path, since the whole health monitor appears to function while doing nothing.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — propagate tool availability explicitly from each runner or from _run_tool returncode/stderr, and in scan_health mark a tool unavailable when invocation returned NOT_FOUND or TIMEOUT instead of treating empty diagnostics as success.

all_findings.description:
FIND — health_trend() produces ragged time series that omit zero-count rounds for categories absent in a scan. It appends counts only for categories present in each scan’s `counts_by_category`; categories missing in a round get no entry. After scans like `{security: 1}` then `{style: 1}`, the returned trend is `{"security": [1], "style": [1]}` instead of aligned per-round series like `{"security": [1,0], "style": [0,1]}`.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing category trends across rounds receives malformed history and can misread disappearance as missing data rather than zero. Since this method exists specifically “for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health,” ragged vectors make trend analysis and thresholding unreliable.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — build the union of categories across scan history and emit one count per round per category, inserting 0 when a category is absent in a given scan.

all_findings.description:
FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is partially dead code. endocrine.py declares DefectCategory.OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION, and the module docstring claims defect classification for “off-by-one” and “race conditions,” but no categoriser path in run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy ever emits either category. All pyright/mypy diagnostics collapse to TYPE_SAFETY or NULL_DEREF; ruff mostly maps to DEAD_CODE/STYLE/SECURITY.
FOLLOW: Downstream, counts_by_category and any reviewer relying on endocrine defect categories will never see those categories fire, so the feature does not deliver the claimed coverage. In a PoC this is medium severity rather than critical, but it is still misleading telemetry and effectively dead functionality.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — either add minimal pattern-based mappings that can actually emit OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION from tool messages, or remove those categories from the advertised capability until supported. The simpler sufficient fix is to stop advertising unsupported categories.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()` marks tools as available whenever the runner function returns normally, even when the binary is missing or timed out. Evidence: `run_pyright()`, `run_ruff()`, `run_bandit()`, and `run_mypy()` all return `[]` on `_run_tool(...).stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`; `scan_health()` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` unconditionally after `diags = runner(existing)`. The same false-positive availability occurs on timeout because `_run_tool()` returns a synthetic `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")`, but the runners mostly just parse empty stdout and return `[]`.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer’s primary contract is to tell the insect brain whether health tooling actually ran. With the current logic, missing/broken analyzers are reported as healthy zero-diagnostic runs. That silently degrades the “health scan” feature into dead infrastructure: reviewers see no diagnostics and no unavailable-tool signal, the insect brain cannot distinguish clean code from non-executed tools, and fix evaluation baselines that reuse these runners can also undercount issues without surfacing that the checker never ran.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — make each runner return both diagnostics and an execution-status flag, or more simply have `_run_tool()` status checked in each runner and raise/propagate a sentinel on `NOT_FOUND`/`TIMEOUT`; then set `tools_available[tool_name] = False` in `scan_health()` for those cases instead of treating empty diagnostics as success.

all_findings.description:
FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is only partially implemented and some declared features never fire. `DefectCategory` includes `OFF_BY_ONE` and `RACE_CONDITION`, and the module docstring promises classification for “off-by-one, race conditions”, but no categoriser path in `_categorise_pyright`, `_categorise_ruff`, `run_bandit`, or `run_mypy` ever emits those categories. `run_crosshair` is also absent despite `CROSSHAIR_BIN` and the top-level docs listing CrossHair.
FOLLOW: This creates dead feature claims in the endocrine interface. The insect brain and human reviewers may assume endocrine is monitoring those defect classes when it never can. At PoC stage that is a misleading-output problem: the feature appears present by API/docs/constants but cannot trigger, reducing trust in the health report and making debugging harder when expected categories stay permanently zero.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — remove unimplemented categories/tool claims from the endocrine interface for now, or wire the simplest real implementation: add a `run_crosshair()` path and only keep categories that current tool parsers can actually emit.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `health_trend()` returns ragged per-category histories and omits zero counts for rounds where a category did not appear. Evidence: it iterates `for scan in self._scan_history: for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. If a category is absent in a round, no `0` is appended, so list positions no longer align to round indices.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing round-over-round trends can misread category trajectories because list index is not stable across rounds. A category sequence like `[5, 1]` may mean rounds 0 and 2, not consecutive rounds. That makes worsening/improving-health logic unreliable and can mis-trigger or miss pacing or human review decisions based on trends.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — build trends over all known categories across all scans and append `scan.counts_by_category.get(cat, 0)` for every round so each category history has one entry per scan.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` claims `context_budget: int` but contains runtime handling for `dict`, then immediately compares `if context_budget > 0:` and divides by it. This is an interface mismatch with the function signature and datamodel. The defensive dict branch implies callers may pass per-model budgets, but the function collapses them to `max(...)`, which understates pressure for smaller-budget models.
FOLLOW: Downstream pacing decisions can be silently wrong in multi-model runs with budget overrides: the endocrine signal may report context as healthy because it uses the largest budget, while one or more models are already near exhaustion. That weakens the insect brain’s degrade/relay decisions and makes the signal misleading.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — make the interface honest: accept only an integer budget in this function and remove the dict branch; callers should pass the actual effective budget they want evaluated.

all_findings.description:
FIND — slow-model and response-size “median” calculations use `sorted(values)[len(values)//2]`, which is not the statistical median for even-sized sets. With 4 or 6 models this selects the upper middle value rather than the average of the two middles. In a 5-model system this is usually fine, but the code is generic and the endocrine layer is infrastructure.
FOLLOW: Threshold-based pacing signals can shift materially around the trigger boundary, especially with an even number of active models after failures. That can suppress legitimate slow-model/context-growth signals or emit spurious ones, affecting relay degradation and timeout adjustments.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — use `statistics.median()` for durations and response sizes.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` novelty plateau detection requires `len(novelty_counts) >= 3 and round_idx >= 2`, then checks `novelty_counts[-3:]`. But `novelty_counts` is passed from the caller as a list where index = round number. If rounds are skipped or the list is shorter than `round_idx`, the check `round_idx >= 2` is redundant with `len(novelty_counts) >= 3`, but more importantly: the condition `all(n <= 1 for n in recent)` triggers on 3 consecutive rounds with ≤1 novel findings. At round 2 (the third round, 0-indexed), with `novelty_counts = [5, 1, 0]`, the plateau fires immediately. Three rounds is very early to declare convergence plateau — this threshold is too aggressive for the typical 6-8 round experiment.

FOLLOW: An overly aggressive novelty plateau signal causes the insect brain to consider convergence too early. If the brain acts on `check_convergence` using this signal, experiments may terminate prematurely before models have fully explored the search space. The signal itself doesn't force termination (it's advisory via `suggested_action="check_convergence"`), so the downstream impact depends on how the insect brain consumes it. Given PoC context, this is MEDIUM — the signal fires too early but doesn't directly break operation.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Change the window from 3 to 4 rounds and require `round_idx >= 3`: `if len(novelty_counts) >= 4 and round_idx >= 3:` with `recent = novelty_counts[-4:]` and `if all(n <= 1 for n in recent):`. This gives models one more round to recover before plateau is signalled.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `EndocrineLayer` has a `health_trend()` method that returns diagnostic count trends across rounds, but it is never called by any code path in the codebase. The insect brain's interface (`insect_brain.py`) does not reference `health_trend()`, and the `EndocrineReport` dataclass doesn't include trend data. The `_scan_history` list grows unboundedly across rounds with no consumer.

FOLLOW: This is dead code that never fires. The health trend feature is documented as "for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health" but the insect brain doesn't consume it. No downstream consequence beyond memory growth from accumulating `HealthScan` objects in `_scan_history`. At PoC scale (6-8 rounds), memory is not a concern.
all_findings.proposed_fix: No fix needed for PoC — this is LOW/documentation-level. If trend detection is wanted, the insect brain needs to call `endo.health_trend()` and use the result.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` receives `context_budget` which may be a dict (per-model budgets). The defensive check `if isinstance(context_budget, dict): context_budget = max(context_budget.values())` extracts the max value. But `cumulative_context_chars` is a single integer representing total chars across all models. Comparing total cumulative chars against a single model's budget is semantically wrong — `context_fraction` will be inflated by the number of models. With 5 models each at 80K budget, cumulative chars of 200K gives `context_fraction = 200000/80000 = 2.5`, triggering the 0.8 threshold when no individual model is anywhere near budget.

FOLLOW: The context_growth pacing signal fires prematurely and persistently once cumulative chars exceed 80% of one model's budget. Since cumulative chars grow roughly linearly with models × rounds, this signal fires after ~1-2 rounds in a 5-model experiment and never stops firing. The insect brain receives `suggested_action="degrade_relay"` every round from early on, which may cause unnecessary context degradation.

FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` slow model detection uses integer division for median: `sorted(durations)[len(durations) // 2]`. With an even number of models (e.g., 4), this picks the element at index 2 (the third-smallest), not the true median (average of elements at indices 1 and 2). The threshold is then `median * 2.5`, which is slightly higher than it should be, making slow model detection marginally less sensitive.

FOLLOW: Minor — the median is off by one rank position for even-length lists. With typical model timings, the practical difference is small. The `> 30.0` second absolute floor provides a safety net. This is not worth fixing at PoC stage.
all_findings.proposed_fix: No fix needed for PoC. If precision matters: `median_duration = sorted(durations)[len(durations) // 2]` is adequate for odd-length lists and a reasonable approximation for even-length.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health` runs pyright, ruff, bandit, and mypy sequentially on every source file between every round. For a multi-file project, this is 4 subprocess invocations per scan. The comment says "they're fast enough on a single file set" but pyright in particular can take 5-15 seconds on first invocation (type inference cache cold start). With 6-8 rounds, that's 4-8 minutes spent on health scans alone.

FOLLOW: Performance impact only — does not affect correctness. At PoC scale with 2-3 source files, this is acceptable. The `_TOOL_TIMEOUT = 60` prevents hangs.
all_findings.proposed_fix: No fix needed for PoC.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_pyright()` records pyright positions without converting from pyright’s 0-based coordinates to the 1-based line numbering used elsewhere in the module (`run_mypy`, `run_bandit`, `run_ruff`) and expected by humans. It stores `rng.get("line", 0)` and `rng.get("character", 0)` directly. Pyright JSON positions are 0-based.
FOLLOW: This yields inconsistent diagnostic coordinates inside a single `HealthScan`: pyright findings point one line earlier than mypy/ruff/bandit. Downstream, `counts_by_file` still works, but any consumer that surfaces line numbers for reviewer action or tries to correlate endocrine diagnostics with findings from the immune/brain layers will mislocate pyright issues. That is a silently misleading output in the health monitor.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — add 1 to pyright line and column values when constructing `ToolDiagnostic`, while keeping 0 only for truly unknown coordinates.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_pyright()` records zero-based line and column numbers from pyright JSON without converting them to the 1-based convention used by the other tool parsers and by most source diagnostics. Code: `line=rng.get("line", 0)`, `column=rng.get("character", 0)`. Pyright’s JSON `range.start.line` / `character` are zero-based. Ruff, Bandit, and mypy paths here all emit 1-based values.
FOLLOW: The health scan then mixes coordinate systems in a single `HealthScan.diagnostics` stream. Any consumer that displays or correlates diagnostics by line number gets silent off-by-one locations for pyright only. That degrades defect triage and can misattribute issues when reviewers compare endocrine output with source lines or other tool findings.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — add 1 to pyright `line` and `character` when populating `ToolDiagnostic`, preserving 0 only when the field is absent.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A mention like `brain.py` will match any source path containing that substring, and a short relative fragment can match multiple files. The function returns the first such path, with no uniqueness check.
FOLLOW: `evaluate_fix()` then patches and evaluates the wrong file while still attributing the verdict to `finding.finding_id`. This produces silently wrong SAFE/HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE results, contaminates immune verification, and can set `verified=True` on a finding whose proposed fix was never applied to its real target.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — require unambiguous resolution: prefer exact normalized path or basename equality among `source_paths`, and if multiple matches remain, return `None` so the fix is UNEVALUABLE instead of patching the wrong file.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()` claims to provide tool availability, but even beyond missing-binary cases already registered, it leaves unavailable tools absent from `tools_available` entirely when `existing` is empty and when a runner returns normally with internal parse failure. Returned `HealthScan.tools_available` is therefore not a stable full map of known tools. Evidence: early return on `if not existing`; aggregate loop only inserts keys for the four iterated tools after calling runners; parse failures inside runners still look “available”.
FOLLOW: Consumers cannot distinguish “tool unavailable”, “tool not run”, and “tool ran but parse failed” from the returned structure. That weakens the endocrine-to-brain contract and makes health reporting misleading, especially when reviewer decisions depend on whether static-analysis coverage actually happened.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — always return all expected tool keys with explicit boolean availability, and separately record execution/parsing status if needed; at minimum initialize all four tool names to `False` before scanning and update only on confirmed execution.

all_findings.description:
FIND — In `compute_pacing_signals`, the Response Size Anomaly detector (check 4) incorrectly sets the `PacingSignal` property to `signal_type="context_growth"` when a model produces an unusually large string (e.g., `rt.response_chars > median_chars * 3`).
FOLLOW: The insect brain will receive ambiguous "context_growth" signals for two distinct conditions: global context budget exhaustion (check 2) and individual model spew (check 4). This prevents targeted mitigations, as the orchestrator cannot distinguish between an experiment nearing its end and a single model breaking constraints.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — Change `signal_type="context_growth"` to `signal_type="response_size_anomaly"` in check 4 of `compute_pacing_signals`.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` check #4 (response size anomaly, lines ~503-512) emits `signal_type="context_growth"`, which is identical to the signal_type used by check #2 (context budget fraction, lines ~487-494). Two semantically distinct conditions produce indistinguishable signals.
FOLLOW: Any downstream consumer (insect brain or orchestrator) that filters or acts on `signal_type` cannot distinguish "overall context budget at 85%" from "one model produced a 30K char response in a single round". If the consumer deduplicates by signal_type, one signal masks the other. If it acts on all instances, a single large response could trigger context degradation even when overall budget usage is low. The `suggested_action` is the same ("degrade_relay") for both, but the appropriate responses are different: budget pressure warrants relay degradation, while a single large response might warrant per-model output capping.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Use a distinct signal_type for check #4:
signals.append(PacingSignal(
    signal_type="response_size_anomaly",
    ...
    suggested_action="cap_model_output",
))

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()` silently drops tool-failure information from totals and counts, so parse failures/timeouts look like a clean scan. Evidence: each runner returns `[]` on `NOT_FOUND`, and on JSON parse failure logs a warning then returns an empty diagnostics list; `_run_tool()` also maps timeout to returncode -1/stderr "TIMEOUT". `scan_health()` aggregates only diagnostics, with no failure counters except a misleading `tools_available` bool already covered in registry. A timeout or malformed output therefore produces `total=0` for that tool, indistinguishable from “no issues found.”
FOLLOW: The insect brain receives a `HealthScan` that can underreport defects during tool failure windows. Combined with inter-round decision-making, this can suppress health deterioration signals and make a broken scanning round appear healthier than the previous one. It also undermines fix evaluation baselines because `_count_tool_issues()` similarly returns `0` on exceptions, biasing verdicts toward SAFE/NEUTRAL.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — add per-tool execution status/failure counts to `HealthScan` and, in fix evaluation, propagate tool execution failure as UNEVALUABLE instead of treating it as zero issues.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` has an interface/type contract mismatch that can crash at runtime when called with non-`int` scalar numerics. The signature says `context_budget: int`, but the implementation only special-cases `dict` and then performs `if context_budget > 0:` followed by division. If a caller passes `None`, a string from config/env parsing, or any other non-int scalar-ish value, this raises `TypeError` inside endocrine between rounds. Evidence: there is no validation/coercion after the dict branch, and `EndocrineLayer.run()` forwards `context_budget` directly.
FOLLOW: This crosses the endocrine→insect-brain pacing interface. A bad config value or override shape aborts pacing computation for the whole round report, which means the endocrine cycle can fail after health scan and fix evaluation have already run. In a PoC this is a HIGH silent integration hazard because pacing is supposed to be a mechanical monitor; instead a malformed budget value can drop the whole endocrine report path rather than degrading to “no context signal”.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — validate/coerce at function entry: after the existing dict handling, require `context_budget` to be an `int` or `float`, otherwise default to `80_000` (or return no context-growth signal). This preserves end-to-end operation without expanding the API surface.

all_findings.description:
FIND — the tool inventory and stated capabilities are internally inconsistent in a way that leaves advertised health-scan features dead. `CROSSHAIR_BIN`, `PYTHON_313`, and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT` are defined; the module header advertises mypy and crosshair binaries; but no crosshair runner exists and `scan_health()` never invokes crosshair. This is distinct from generic category dead code: an entire listed analyzer is unreachable.
FOLLOW: Downstream health reports systematically omit one of the declared analyzers while still presenting as a full “whole-body health monitor”. That misleads reviewers about coverage and can skew pacing/health decisions if they assume symbolic execution is contributing. For PoC this is MEDIUM but quick to fix because it is pure interface honesty.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — remove crosshair from the documented/tool constant surface for now (and delete unused constants), or add it to `scan_health()` with a minimal runner. The simpler PoC correction is to remove the dead advertised support.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The endocrine layer’s pacing‑signal function `compute_pacing_signals` contains a logic error in slow‑model detection that can cause division by zero. The code calculates `median_duration = sorted(durations)[len(durations) // 2]`. If `durations` is empty (possible when `round_timings` is empty or contains only zero‑duration entries), this indexing raises `IndexError`. The function catches exceptions only for convergence metrics, not for this median calculation.
EVIDENCE: Lines ~475‑485: `if round_timings:` guard passes if `round_timings` is a non‑empty list, but `durations` could be `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]`. `len(durations) // 2` is 1, indexing works. However, if `round_timings` is `[]`, the guard skips the block. The bug triggers when `round_timings` is provided but all durations are zero (unlikely but possible). The more critical issue is the missing exception handling for the median calculation itself.
FOLLOW: An uncaught `IndexError` would crash the endocrine layer between rounds, halting the entire CDSFL bench. The insect brain would not receive pacing signals, potentially disrupting round‑timing decisions. This is a CRITICAL failure path for end‑to‑end operation.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Add a defensive check inside the slow‑model detection block: `if durations:` before calculating the median. If `durations` is empty, skip slow‑model detection entirely. Additionally, use `try‑except` around the median calculation to catch any unexpected errors and log them without crashing.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The endocrine layer’s `run_pyright` function mis‑categorizes all pyright diagnostics as `TYPE_SAFETY` or `NULL_DEREF`. The categorisation logic `_categorise_pyright` uses keyword matching that incorrectly labels other error types (e.g., “reportMissingImports”, “reportUnknownMemberType”) as type safety. This inflates the `type_safety` count in `HealthScan` and misleads the insect brain’s health trends.
EVIDENCE: `_categorise_pyright` checks for keywords “none”, “optional”, “could be none”, “is not callable” → `NULL_DEREF`; otherwise defaults to `TYPE_SAFETY`. Pyright produces many other diagnostic types (import errors, syntax errors, attribute errors) that should be mapped to `UNKNOWN` or more specific categories. The current mapping skews defect‑distribution metrics.
FOLLOW: The insect brain uses `counts_by_category` to track code‑health trends. Inflated type‑safety counts may trigger false alarms or mask real trends in other categories. For PoC, this is a MEDIUM issue—it does not break end‑to‑end operation but degrades the quality of health signals.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Expand categorisation to map known pyright rule prefixes: `"reportMissingImports"` → `UNKNOWN`, `"reportUnknownMemberType"` → `TYPE_SAFETY`, `"reportUnnecessaryComparison"` → `STYLE`. For un‑matched rules, default to `UNKNOWN`. This preserves the existing NULL_DEREF detection.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `CROSSHAIR_BIN` and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT` are declared (lines ~47, 52) but no `run_crosshair()` function exists and crosshair is never invoked anywhere in the module. Similarly, `PYTHON_313` is declared (line ~48) but never used. These are dead declarations that suggest planned features that were never implemented.

FOLLOW: No functional impact — these are unused constants. However, `CROSSHAIR_BIN` and `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT` create the impression that symbolic execution is available as a verification tool, which could mislead someone reading the module header (which lists crosshair as a tool binary). The insect brain doesn't reference these constants. No downstream breakage.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Remove `CROSSHAIR_BIN`, `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT`, and `PYTHON_313` declarations, and remove crosshair from the module docstring's tool list. Three lines deleted.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()`’s public contract says `source_paths` are “Absolute paths to Python source files”, but the implementation only filters `os.path.isfile(p)` and passes every existing file to pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy. Non-Python files are therefore analyzed if accidentally included. Since bandit/pyright/mypy are Python-oriented, this can generate parse noise, empty output, or tool-specific failures that are counted as code-health signals for the wrong artifact set.
FOLLOW: the health scan becomes interface-fragile with the insect brain/orchestrator: one bad path in the shared `source_paths` list can distort diagnostics and pacing decisions between rounds. In a PoC this is high enough to matter because the endocrine report is meant to be mechanical and trustworthy, not dependent on callers perfectly honoring an undocumented precondition.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — enforce the contract in `scan_health()` by filtering to existing `.py` files only before invoking tools.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_run_tool` returns `TIMEOUT` in stderr on timeout, but the tool runners (`run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, etc.) treat this as a successful execution (return empty list) and `scan_health` marks the tool as available. This causes silent loss of static‑analysis results when a tool times out, and the health scan will incorrectly report zero diagnostics from that tool.  
EVIDENCE: In `_run_tool`, `sp.TimeoutExpired` is caught and returns `stderr="TIMEOUT"`. In `run_pyright`, the check `if result.stderr == "NOT_FOUND":` does not catch `"TIMEOUT"`, so the function proceeds to parse the empty stdout and returns `[]`. `scan_health` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True`. The same pattern occurs in `run_ruff`, `run_bandit`, `run_mypy`.  
FOLLOW:  
1. The insect brain receives a health scan that under‑reports true defect counts, potentially causing it to signal convergence prematurely.  
2. The endocrine layer’s primary function (health monitoring) is compromised because a critical verification tool is effectively offline but reported as healthy.  
3. Downstream fix evaluation may also be affected because `_count_tool_issues` calls the same runners; a timeout will return 0 issues, making a harmful fix appear safe.  
4. This bug is a direct extension of C0001/C0004 (missing binary) but adds the timeout case, which is more likely in practice given tool timeouts.
all_findings.proposed_fix: In each tool runner, after checking for `"NOT_FOUND"`, also check for `"TIMEOUT"` and return an empty list (or treat as unavailable). Additionally, `scan_health` should set `tools_available[tool_name] = False` for timeout or not‑found conditions. The simplest fix: modify `_run_tool` to return a structured result (e.g., a dict with `status`, `output`, `stderr`) and have runners propagate the status, or have runners return `(diagnostics, available)` where `available` is `False` on `"NOT_FOUND"` or `"TIMEOUT"`.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The endocrine layer’s pacing‑signal function `compute_pacing_signals` uses a hard‑coded threshold of 0.8 (80%) for context‑growth signaling, but the context budget may be as low as 20,000 characters in some experiments. At that budget, 80% is 16,000 characters, which may be reached in the first round, causing premature “degrade_relay” signals. The threshold is not calibrated to the actual budget and may be too sensitive for small‑budget runs.  
EVIDENCE: Line ~468: `if context_fraction > 0.8:` with `context_fraction = cumulative_context_chars / context_budget`. The threshold 0.8 is arbitrary and not configurable.  
FOLLOW:  
1. Early “degrade_relay” signals may force the insect brain into summary‑only mode too soon, reducing cross‑pollination and potentially slowing convergence.  
2. For small‑budget experiments, this could trigger in round 1, effectively disabling the conversational relay from the start.  
3. The pacing signal is meant to guide convergence, but an overly sensitive threshold may hinder it.  
4. This is a design flaw that affects the experiment’s efficiency but not correctness.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Make the threshold configurable (e.g., via `EndocrineLayer` constructor) or adjust it dynamically based on the budget size (e.g., use 0.9 for budgets > 50k, 0.95 for smaller budgets). For PoC, the simplest fix is to raise the threshold to 0.9 to reduce false positives.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_mypy` uses a regex to parse mypy output, but mypy can emit multi‑line messages (e.g., with note lines). The regex `^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?$` matches only single lines, causing note lines to be ignored or mis‑parsed. This leads to under‑counting of mypy diagnostics.  
EVIDENCE: The regex is compiled with no `re.DOTALL` flag and matches per line. Mypy often outputs note lines indented with spaces, which will not match the pattern and will be skipped.  
FOLLOW:  
1. The health scan will report fewer mypy errors than actually exist, misleading the insect brain about code health.  
2. Fix evaluation may incorrectly assess the impact of a fix on type safety because the baseline mypy count is incomplete.  
3. This bug reduces the effectiveness of mypy as a verification tool in the endocrine layer.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Use mypy’s `--no‑error‑summary` and `--show‑column‑numbers` flags (already present) and parse each line as before, but also accumulate note lines that belong to the previous error. Alternatively, use mypy’s `--json‑output` flag (if available) for structured parsing.

all_findings.description:
FIND — the advertised “health scan — static analysis (pyright/ruff/bandit) between rounds” never reports explicit tool failure diagnostics. When a tool times out, is missing, or emits unparsable output, runners mostly return `[]` and `scan_health()` just aggregates zero diagnostics. Apart from logging, the returned `HealthScan` has no field for execution failure/parse failure counts, so a broken scanner can look identical to a clean codebase.
FOLLOW: This degrades the endocrine layer’s primary role as a health monitor: the insect brain and human reviewer receive “0 diagnostics” without machine-readable evidence that the scan itself failed. Combined with the known availability bug, this can make the monitoring layer fail open and hide that no meaningful scan occurred.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — add minimal machine-readable scan failure reporting to `HealthScan` (e.g. per-tool status/error string) and populate it from each runner on NOT_FOUND/TIMEOUT/parse failure instead of silently returning empty diagnostics.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The endocrine layer has no error recovery or fallback when tool binaries are missing or crash. If `pyright` is not installed, `run_pyright` returns empty diagnostics and `tools_available["pyright"] = True` (due to missing NOT_FOUND check, see C0001). The health scan proceeds as if the tool succeeded, producing a false “clean” signal. The insect brain may then incorrectly assume the codebase is healthy.
FOLLOW: Missing tools lead to silent false negatives in health scans. The insect brain’s decisions (e.g., to degrade relay, check convergence) rely on accurate health metrics; corrupted metrics may cause inappropriate pacing signals.
all_findings.proposed_fix: In `_run_tool`, set a distinct stderr string for each failure mode (NOT_FOUND, TIMEOUT, CRASH). In each tool runner, check for these strings and return empty diagnostics + log an error. In `scan_health`, set `tools_available[tool_name] = False` if the runner returns empty diagnostics due to failure (requires runners to return a status flag). Alternatively, have `_run_tool` raise a custom exception that the runner catches to set availability=False.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` divides by `context_budget` without checking for zero. If `context_budget` is 0 (possible when the dict is empty or the config value is zero), the line `context_fraction = cumulative_context_chars / context_budget` raises `ZeroDivisionError`. This crashes the endocrine cycle, halting the experiment.
FOLLOW: A crash in the endocrine layer prevents the insect brain from receiving any health or pacing signals for that round. The brain may continue with stale or empty signals, potentially making incorrect convergence decisions.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Add a guard: `if context_budget <= 0: return signals` (or set `context_fraction = 1.0` to force a context‑growth signal). Ensure the default config value is positive.

all_findings.description:
FIND — Response‑size anomaly detection fails when all models produce zero‑length responses. The code filters `char_counts = [rt.response_chars for rt in round_timings if rt.response_chars > 0]`. If all responses are empty, `char_counts` is empty, and `median_chars = sorted(char_counts)[len(char_counts) // 2]` raises `IndexError`.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer crashes, breaking the pacing signal generation. The insect brain does not receive pacing signals, potentially affecting relay decisions.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Check that `char_counts` is non‑empty before computing median. If empty, skip the response‑size check.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()` runs all four static analysis tools sequentially on every source file between every round. For a medium‑sized codebase (e.g., 10 files), this may take 10‑30 seconds per round, adding significant overhead to the experiment timeline. The PoC goal is “shipped for human review as quickly as possible”; this delay is contrary to that goal.
FOLLOW: Lengthened round duration reduces the number of rounds possible within a fixed wall‑clock budget, potentially preventing convergence before budget exhaustion. It also increases the risk of timeouts in the overall experiment orchestration.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Cache tool results per file hash (or modification timestamp) and only re‑run tools when source files have changed. Since the codebase is static during a multi‑model review, a single health scan per experiment is sufficient. Modify `EndocrineLayer.run()` to skip the health scan after the first round unless `source_paths` have changed.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The `PacingSignal` dataclass has a field `suggested_action` that is never used. The insect brain receives the signals but does not act on the suggested action; it only logs them. This is dead code that misleads readers about the system’s capabilities.
FOLLOW: No operational impact, but adds unnecessary complexity and confusion for future maintainers.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Remove the `suggested_action` field from `PacingSignal` and from the signal‑construction calls. The insect brain already has hard‑coded logic to map signal types to actions; the field is redundant.

all_findings.description:
FIND — Docstring for `EndocrineLayer` claims it provides “4. Pacing signals — monitor timing, context growth, novelty plateau”. The novelty plateau detection uses `novelty_counts` from the insect brain, but there is no explanation of what “novelty” means or how the counts are derived. This is a documentation gap, not a code bug.
FOLLOW: Developers extending the endocrine layer may misunderstand the input contract and provide incorrect novelty counts, leading to false pacing signals.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Extend the docstring of `compute_pacing_signals()` to clarify: “`novelty_counts` is a list of novel finding counts per round, where novelty is defined by the convergence detector’s equivalence‑class deduplication.”

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` novelty plateau check ignores the `round_idx` window it claims to evaluate and instead always uses `novelty_counts[-3:]`. If the caller passes a longer history than the current round index represents, the function evaluates future/extra entries rather than rounds ending at `round_idx`. Evidence: current code gates on `round_idx >= 2` but slices the tail of the full list, not `novelty_counts[max(0, round_idx-2):round_idx+1]`.
FOLLOW: Pacing signals are consumed by the insect brain for convergence/timing decisions. Using the wrong rounds can emit or suppress `novelty_plateau` at the wrong time, causing premature convergence checks or missed plateau detection. This does not usually crash the PoC, but it can distort inter-round control flow and reviewer-visible pacing behavior.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — compute the recent window from `round_idx` explicitly: use the three entries ending at `round_idx`, and only evaluate when `len(novelty_counts) > round_idx`.

all_findings.description:
FIND — the advertised “Health scan — static analysis (pyright/ruff/bandit) between rounds” does not actually surface tool execution failure as a diagnostic or status field separate from availability. When a tool times out or emits unparsable output, runners return `[]` and `scan_health()` just aggregates an empty result set. Aside from the already-registered availability bug, there is no diagnostic record or failure counter telling the caller that the scan was incomplete. Evidence: parse failures only log warnings; `HealthScan` contains counts and `tools_available` but no per-tool run status / error reason.
FOLLOW: A zero-diagnostic health scan can mean “clean code” or “tool failed,” and the insect brain receives no machine-readable distinction. That can suppress pacing/escalation decisions tied to code health and makes the endocrine report misleading during infrastructure failures. In PoC terms this is a silent wrong result in the monitoring layer, because the feature appears to fire cleanly while having skipped analysis.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — add a minimal per-tool status field to `HealthScan` (e.g. `tool_status[tool] = "ok" | "not_found" | "timeout" | "parse_error" | "failed"`) and populate it from `_run_tool` / runner parse branches so incomplete scans are explicitly visible.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_mypy` uses a brittle regex to parse mypy output. Mypy can emit multi‑line errors (e.g., note lines) and the regex `^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?$` captures only the first line, discarding subsequent note lines. This under‑reports mypy diagnostics and misrepresents code health.  
FOLLOW: The health scan aggregates incomplete mypy results, causing the insect brain to receive falsely low defect counts. This could delay convergence (if novelty counts are artificially low) or miss critical type errors. The endocrine layer’s primary health signal is corrupted.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Use mypy’s `--output-format=json` (available in mypy ≥0.990) to get structured output. Fall back to regex only if JSON fails. Example:  
cmd = [MYPY_BIN, "--output-format=json", "--no-color-output", "--show-column-numbers", "--no-error-summary"] + paths
Parse the JSON array of diagnostics, extracting file, line, column, severity, message, and error code.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health` runs four tools sequentially on every source file each round. For a large codebase, this could exceed the inter‑round time budget. No parallelism, no incremental analysis.  
FOLLOW: If health scan takes longer than the round interval, it delays the insect brain’s decision loop, slowing convergence. For PoC with small files it may be fine, but the design does not scale.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Run tool invocations in parallel using `concurrent.futures`. Keep the same timeout per tool. Aggregate results after all finish.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `ToolDiagnostic.severity` is a free‑form string (pyright uses `"error"`, `"warning"`, `"information"`; mypy uses `"error"`, `"warning"`, `"note"`; bandit maps `"LOW"`→`"info"`, etc.). Inconsistent severity strings break `counts_by_severity` aggregation (e.g., `"information"` vs `"info"`).  
FOLLOW: The health scan’s severity counts are fragmented, misleading the insect brain about error vs warning ratios. This could affect pacing signals (e.g., if severity thresholds are added later).
all_findings.proposed_fix: Normalize severity values: map pyright’s `"information"`→`"info"`, bandit’s `"LOW"`→`"info"`, `"MEDIUM"`→`"warning"`, `"HIGH"`→`"error"`. Keep mypy’s `"note"` as `"info"`. Use a dict mapping per tool.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `EndocrineLayer.run` accepts `novelty_counts` list but does not validate its length matches `round_idx`. If the list is shorter, the novelty‑plateau check accesses out‑of‑bounds indices (`novelty_counts[-3:]` when `len(novelty_counts) < 3`).  
FOLLOW: The plateau detection will crash or produce incorrect signals, causing the insect brain to miss a convergence cue.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Guard with `if len(novelty_counts) >= 3:` before accessing `[-3:]`. Also, ensure `round_idx` consistency (should be `len(novelty_counts)`).

all_findings.description:
FIND — the health scan feature does not actually run all tools promised by the module contract. The file header and constants advertise `crosshair` and `mypy`, but `scan_health()` only invokes pyright, ruff, bandit, and mypy; there is no `run_crosshair()` and no CrossHair execution path anywhere in `endocrine.py`. This is distinct from the existing dead-constant report because the externally documented “Health scan — static analysis (pyright/ruff/bandit)” plus top-level tool list implies a working tool path that never fires.
FOLLOW: Downstream, any consumer trusting endocrine’s tool coverage will assume symbolic execution contributed to the health signal when it did not. That weakens defect detection for path-sensitive bugs and makes tool-availability accounting incomplete, because `tools_available` never reports crosshair at all despite the advertised capability.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — remove CrossHair from the documented/declared health-scan tool set for the PoC until an actual `run_crosshair()` integration exists.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` slow-model detection (lines ~473-483) computes median then checks `rt.duration_s > median_duration * 2.5 and rt.duration_s > 30.0`. With a single model (`len(round_timings) == 1`), the median equals that model's duration, so `duration > duration * 2.5` is always false. Slow-model detection is dead for single-model runs. With two models, the "median" is `sorted([a,b])[1]` = the larger value, so the slower model is compared against itself and can never trigger.

FOLLOW: This is partially covered by C0018 (single-model case) and C0008/C0012 (median calculation). However, the *two-model* case is not covered: integer division `len(durations) // 2` for 2 items gives index 1, which is the *maximum*, not the median. The slower of two models is compared against itself. Slow-model detection requires ≥3 models to function at all.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Already addressed by C0008's fix (`statistics.median`). No separate fix needed — filing for completeness of the two-model edge case.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_pyright()` loses diagnostics on the normal “errors found” path when pyright writes JSON to stderr instead of stdout. `_run_tool()` captures both streams, but `run_pyright()` only parses `result.stdout` and ignores `result.stderr` except for the sentinel `"NOT_FOUND"`. Many CLIs emit machine-readable output to stderr on nonzero exit; this wrapper assumes stdout-only and turns such runs into parse failure + empty diagnostics.
FOLLOW: The health scan can report zero pyright findings even though pyright executed and found issues. In fix evaluation, pre/post type-error baselines also become wrong, so `_compute_fix_verdict()` can misclassify patches. This affects both major endocrine outputs: `HealthScan` and `FixEvaluation`, and can flow into immune Stage 4 verified-fix marking.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — in `run_pyright()`, choose the JSON payload from `result.stdout` if non-empty, otherwise from `result.stderr` when it looks like JSON; parse that payload instead of stdout only.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_categorise_pyright` and `_categorise_ruff` use substring matching on lowercased messages, which is fragile and may misclassify. For example, `"cannot assign"` matches `"cannot assign"` but also `"cannot assignable"` (non‑existent). The categorisation logic does not use pyright’s `rule` field, which provides stable identifiers.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequences:
1. Misclassified diagnostics lead to incorrect `counts_by_category` aggregates.
2. The insect brain may make incorrect decisions based on skewed defect category trends.
3. The health trend data becomes noisy and less useful for convergence detection.
4. If the endocrine layer is extended to act on specific defect categories, misclassification will cause wrong actions.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Use pyright’s `rule` field for categorisation. Map known rule prefixes to defect categories (e.g., `"reportMissingImports"` → `UNKNOWN`, `"reportUnusedVariable"` → `DEAD_CODE`). For ruff, use the code prefix (F, E, W, S, B) as already done, but refine based on known code patterns. Add a default `UNKNOWN` category for unhandled rules.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` does not guard against negative `novelty_counts` values. If the novelty count is negative (possible due to a bug elsewhere), the condition `all(n <= 1 for n in recent)` will incorrectly trigger a novelty plateau signal because negative numbers are ≤1.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequences:
1. A negative novelty count (indicating a bug) will be misinterpreted as zero novelty, triggering a false plateau signal.
2. The insect brain may incorrectly think convergence has been reached and signal early termination.
3. The experiment may stop prematurely, missing critical findings.
4. The endocrine layer’s pacing signals become unreliable.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Add a sanity check: `if any(n < 0 for n in recent): return signals` (or log a warning and skip the plateau detection). Also, clamp novelty counts to non-negative in the caller.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health` runs all four tools sequentially on every source file every round, with no caching. For a large codebase (e.g., 100 files), this could take minutes, delaying rounds. The PoC context accepts this, but the endocrine layer is meant to run between rounds; excessive delay breaks the pacing.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequences:
1. Round duration increases significantly, causing the experiment to run longer than necessary.
2. The slow-model detection may trigger falsely because the endocrine layer itself is slow.
3. Context growth may accelerate due to longer rounds, causing premature degradation.
4. The insect brain’s timing data becomes skewed by endocrine overhead.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Implement simple caching by file modification timestamp. Compute a hash of each source file’s content (or use `os.path.getmtime`). If the file hasn’t changed since the last scan, reuse the previous diagnostics for that file. Only run tools on changed files. Cache results in `EndocrineLayer` instance.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The docstring for `EndocrineLayer` claims it provides “4. Pacing signals — monitor timing, context growth, novelty plateau monitoring”, but the `novelty_counts` parameter is not explained. The caller must provide a list of novel finding counts per round, but it’s unclear how to compute that.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequences:
1. Developers integrating the endocrine layer may pass incorrect novelty counts, causing false plateau signals.
2. The insect brain may receive misleading pacing signals, affecting round decisions.
3. The endocrine layer’s pacing signals become unreliable.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Extend the docstring of `compute_pacing_signals` and `EndocrineLayer.run` to clarify: “`novelty_counts` is a list of novel finding counts per round, where index 0 corresponds to round 0. Novel findings are those not deduplicated against prior rounds (typically from the immune pipeline’s NK cell).”

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_find_target_file` (lines ~370-385) uses a loose regex `r"[\w/\\]+\.py\b"` to extract file paths from finding descriptions, then falls back to `source_paths[0]` when no match is found. The regex matches any word-chars followed by `.py` — including fragments like `t.py` or `self.py` embedded in natural language. The `match in sp_path` containment check (line ~382) means a short fragment like `s.py` would match any source path containing that substring (e.g., `bench/immune_agents.py`). When no regex match is found, the fallback to `source_paths[0]` means fixes are evaluated against whichever file happens to be first in the list, regardless of which file the finding actually targets.

FOLLOW: A finding about `insect_brain.py` could be evaluated against `immune_agents.py` (or whatever `source_paths[0]` is). The fix is applied to the wrong file's source text, likely fails to match any code (`_apply_fix_to_source` returns None), and the verdict is UNEVALUABLE. In the false-match case (short fragment matches wrong file), the fix is applied to the wrong file — if it happens to apply (e.g., both files contain similar patterns), the pre/post comparison is on the wrong file entirely, producing a meaningless verdict that gets propagated as ground truth.

FIND — sandbox application loses package structure by writing the patched file to `tmpdir/os.path.basename(target_path)`. If the original file lives under a package path such as `bench/endocrine.py`, the sandboxed file becomes just `endocrine.py`, so static-analysis and any imports evaluate a different module path context from the real codebase. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no recreation of parent directories and no copy of package metadata like `bench/__init__.py` or sibling modules.
FOLLOW: Downstream, pyright/ruff/bandit results on the patched file are not representative of the real integration context. Import-based diagnostics may disappear or appear spuriously; relative imports and package-qualified references are evaluated under the wrong path. This makes the endocrine layer’s core promise — “does the proposed fix break anything?” — mechanically unreliable, and that unreliability flows into immune verification and closed-bug state.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — recreate the original relative path inside the temp directory and write the patch there, preserving package layout.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()` does not report unavailable tools for tools that are skipped due to missing binaries unless an exception is raised. Existing registry already covers the generic availability bug, but there is a second interface hole: the returned `tools_available` map omits tools entirely when `existing` is empty, and omits any tool not iterated or failed before assignment. Consumers therefore cannot distinguish “tool unavailable”, “tool not run”, and “healthy zero diagnostics” from the report shape itself. Evidence: early return `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` with default empty `tools_available`; within the loop, keys are added only after runner returns or exception occurs.
FOLLOW: Downstream, callers that rely on `tools_available` as a completeness indicator cannot tell whether the endocrine scan truly covered pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy in a round. For a PoC whole-body monitor, that can mask complete loss of monitoring on empty/misresolved path sets and produce misleading infrastructure health reports.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — always initialise `tools_available` with all expected tool keys set to `False`, then flip to `True` only on confirmed successful invocation.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The endocrine layer’s pacing‑signal thresholds are static and not calibrated to the experiment scale, causing false positives/negatives in a PoC environment. The thresholds: slow‑model = 30s absolute, 2.5× median; context‑growth = 80% of budget; novelty‑plateau = zero findings for 3 rounds; response‑size anomaly = 3× median and >10k chars. These are hard‑coded (lines 487, 494, 501, 510) and may be too sensitive for small PoC runs (e.g., a 10‑second round is “slow” if median is 4s). Evidence: lines 487–512 show magic numbers with no configuration.  
FOLLOW: Downstream:  
1. False slow‑model signals may cause the orchestrator to increase timeouts unnecessarily, wasting compute.  
2. False context‑growth signals may trigger relay degradation prematurely, reducing cross‑pollination.  
3. False novelty‑plateau signals may signal convergence too early, terminating the experiment before all bugs are found.  
4. The insect brain receives noisy pacing signals, potentially making poor round‑to‑round decisions.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Make thresholds configurable via `EndocrineLayer` constructor parameters with sensible defaults. For PoC, relax thresholds: slow‑model absolute threshold to 60s; context‑growth threshold to 90%; novelty‑plateau window to 4 rounds with ≤1 finding; response‑size threshold to 5× median and >20k chars. Add a comment that these are PoC‑tuned.  
PROPOSED_FIX (code):  
def __init__(self, source_paths, test_cmd=None, max_fix_evals=20,
             slow_abs_thresh=60.0, slow_rel_thresh=2.5,
             context_growth_thresh=0.9, novelty_plateau_rounds=4,
             novelty_plateau_max=1, response_rel_thresh=5.0,
             response_abs_thresh=20000):
    # … store thresholds …
Then use these in `compute_pacing_signals`.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_mypy`’s regex fails to capture the error‑code when mypy outputs `[error‑code]` with internal spaces or multiple codes. The regex `r"^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?$"` (line 301) assumes the code is a single token inside brackets. Mypy can output `[attr‑defined]` or `[union‑attr, no‑untyped‑def]`. Evidence: line 301; the capture group `(.+?)` stops at first space, splitting `union‑attr, no‑untyped‑def` into only `union‑attr,`.  
FOLLOW: Downstream:  
1. Error codes are truncated, losing fidelity in diagnostic categorization.  
2. The defect‑category mapping (which might use error codes) becomes unreliable.  
3. The health‑scan aggregate counts by code are inaccurate.  
4. Downstream analysis (e.g., trend detection) may misinterpret error types.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Adjust regex to capture everything between `[` and `]` until end of line. Change to:  
pattern = re.compile(
    r"^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?$"
)
Wait, that’s the existing pattern. The issue is `(.+?)` is non‑greedy and stops at space. Use `(.+?)` but allow spaces: actually, `(.+?)` already matches spaces because `.` matches space. The problem is the `?` makes it stop at the first `]`. Change to `(.+?)` with a lookahead for `]`. Simpler: use `r"^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[([^\]]+)\])?$"`.  
PROPOSED_FIX (code):  
pattern = re.compile(
    r"^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note):\s+(.+?)(?:\s+\[([^\]]+)\])?$"
)

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health` runs all four static‑analysis tools sequentially on every source file every round, regardless of whether files changed. For a PoC with 10+ source files, this adds 10–30 seconds per round, slowing convergence. Evidence: lines 340‑360: loops over tools, each calls `runner(existing)`; no caching of file hashes/modification times.  
FOLLOW: Downstream:  
1. Increased round duration extends experiment wall‑clock time.  
2. The insect brain’s pacing signals may incorrectly flag “slow model” due to endocrine overhead.  
3. Resource contention with concurrent model runs (if any).  
4. For PoC, the delay is acceptable but wasteful; in scaled runs, it becomes a bottleneck.

FIND — `run_ruff` parses the `location` field from ruff's JSON output using `loc.get("row", 0)` and `loc.get("column", 0)`. However, ruff's `--output-format=json` returns a nested structure where the location is at `issue["location"]["row"]` for the start position, and `issue["end_location"]["row"]` for the end. The code correctly accesses `location.row/column`, but ruff's JSON schema changed across versions. In ruff ≥0.1.0, the field is `location` with `row`/`column`. In some versions, the top-level keys differ. More critically, the code does not handle the case where `result.stdout` is empty string — `json.loads("")` raises `JSONDecodeError`, which is caught, but the empty-check `if result.stdout.strip()` uses a ternary that falls through to `[]`, which is correct. Actually this parses fine. Let me revise: the actual issue is that ruff exit code 0 means no issues, exit code 1 means issues found, exit code 2 means an error. The code doesn't distinguish between "issues found" (valid JSON on stdout) and "ruff internal error" (error message on stderr, possibly no JSON on stdout). On internal error, `json.loads` of stderr garbage or empty stdout → caught by except → returns `[]` → scan_health marks ruff as available.

FOLLOW: This overlaps with C0001/C0004 (tool availability misreporting) but adds a distinct failure mode: ruff internal errors are silently swallowed and reported as "0 findings, tool available." The insect brain sees a clean ruff report when ruff actually crashed.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Already addressed by C0004's fix (check `_run_tool` return status). Withdrawing as independent finding.

SUPERSEDES: — (withdrawn, subsumed by C0004)

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` slow-model detection (line ~468) computes median from all durations including zero-duration entries. If a model fails instantly (duration_s ≈ 0), the median is pulled down, and normal-duration models appear "slow" relative to a near-zero median. With `median_duration * 2.5` as the threshold, a 0.1s median means any model taking >0.25s AND >30s triggers — the 30s floor catches the worst case, but with 2-3 fast failures and 2 normal models, the median can be low enough that the 30s floor is the only protection.

FOLLOW: The insect brain receives spurious `slow_model` pacing signals for models that are performing normally. If the insect brain acts on these signals (e.g., increasing timeouts or degrading relay), it makes unnecessary adjustments. In practice, the 30s absolute floor prevents the worst outcome, but the signal is still misleading metadata in the endocrine report.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Filter out zero-duration entries before computing median, or use only models with `duration_s > 1.0`:
durations = [rt.duration_s for rt in round_timings if rt.duration_s > 1.0]
if not durations:
    durations = [rt.duration_s for rt in round_timings]

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring containment instead of an exact/relative-path match. Evidence: it extracts `*.py` substrings from finding text, then returns the first `source_path` where `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. The `match in sp_path` branch is unsafe: a mention like `brain.py` matches `/repo/bench/insect_brain.py`; `endocrine.py` could match a backup path containing that token; short names collide across modules.
FOLLOW: Wrong target-file selection makes fix evaluation operate on unrelated code. Baseline counts are taken from one file, the patch is applied to another, and the verdict is still attributed to `finding.finding_id`. Downstream, the immune pipeline may mark a fix verified for the wrong bug, and the sandbox signal becomes deceptive rather than merely noisy. Because endocrine is used as infrastructure between rounds, this kind of mis-targeting can silently poison multiple rounds of verification.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — remove the broad `match in sp_path` heuristic and match only on normalized exact basename equality or full relative-path suffix equality (`endswith(os.sep + match)` or exact basename match when unique). If no unique match exists, return `None` so the evaluation becomes `UNEVALUABLE` instead of patching the wrong file.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_mypy()` can silently return zero diagnostics on normal mypy failure modes because it parses only stdout with a narrow regex and ignores stderr/exit-status-driven fatal messages. Evidence: after `_run_tool(cmd)`, the function checks only `result.stderr == "NOT_FOUND"` and then iterates `for line in result.stdout.splitlines()`. Any invocation/config error or fatal message emitted on stderr yields `[]`, which is indistinguishable from “no mypy issues”.
FOLLOW: In `scan_health()`, this undercounts type diagnostics and makes the health monitor claim a healthier codebase than observed. In `evaluate_fix()`, pre/post mypy is not used, but the main advertised health scan is affected: reviewers and pacing logic consuming `HealthScan` can miss genuine typing failures if mypy reports via stderr. This is especially problematic because the module claims mechanical extraction from tool execution, but here stderr-based failures collapse to clean health.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — in `run_mypy()`, if stdout produced no parsed diagnostics and stderr is non-empty (other than `NOT_FOUND`/`TIMEOUT` handling already tracked elsewhere), emit one `ToolDiagnostic` representing a mypy execution/parsing failure with category `UNKNOWN` and severity `error`, using stderr text as the message.

all_findings.description:
FIND — ToolDiagnostic severity mapping inconsistent: pyright uses "error"/"warning"/"info"; ruff uses "warning" for everything; bandit maps LOW→"info", MEDIUM→"warning", HIGH→"error". This makes `counts_by_severity` aggregates misleading. A bandit HIGH severity appears as "error", ruff error appears as "warning". Insect brain cannot distinguish true errors from warnings.
FOLLOW: Insect brain's health signals (e.g., error count threshold) may trigger incorrectly. If ruff reports 100 style violations as "warning" and pyright reports 1 type error as "error", the aggregate shows 1 error, 100 warnings — misrepresents health.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Normalize severity across tools: map each tool's levels to common scale (ERROR, WARNING, INFO). Or keep raw but document mapping.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_find_target_file()` arbitrarily defaults to returning `source_paths[0]` if it cannot match a filename from the finding's description text.
FOLLOW: If a finding describes a fix without explicitly mentioning a `.py` filename, it silently falls back to the first file in `source_paths`. If the proposed fix is a complete file replacement (Strategy 2 in `_apply_fix_to_source`), it will blindly overwrite `source_paths[0]` with code intended for a completely different module. This will catastrophically break the sandbox tests, leading to a spurious `HARMFUL` verdict while wasting compute resources evaluating the wrong file entirely.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — Change the fallback in `_find_target_file()` to return `None` (or only fallback to the first file if `len(source_paths) == 1`). `evaluate_fix()` already safely handles a `None` target path by marking the fix as `UNEVALUABLE`.

all_findings.description:
FIND — Tool runners (`run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, `run_bandit`, `run_mypy`) silently swallow tool execution failures, returning empty diagnostics while marking tools as available. When a tool exits with a non-zero code due to an internal error (e.g., syntax error in source, missing module, out-of-memory), the runner logs a JSON parse warning but still returns an empty list. The `scan_health` function then incorrectly marks the tool as `True` in `tools_available`. Evidence: In `run_pyright`, if `json.loads(result.stdout)` fails (JSONDecodeError), the function logs a warning and returns `[]`. No check of `result.stderr` for error messages. Same pattern in `run_ruff`, `run_bandit`, and `run_mypy`.
FOLLOW: This leads to incorrect health metrics: missing diagnostics, inflated tool availability, and misleading health signals to the insect brain. Downstream, `evaluate_fix` uses `_count_tool_issues` which calls these same runners; if a tool fails silently, the fix evaluation will see 0 issues pre- and post-fix, leading to incorrect `NEUTRAL` or `SAFE` verdicts. The insect brain may incorrectly conclude code health is improving when tools are actually failing.
all_findings.proposed_fix:
Add explicit error detection in each runner: after the `"NOT_FOUND"` and `"TIMEOUT"` checks, examine `result.stderr` for indications of tool failure (non-empty stderr that isn't a known warning pattern). If present, log an error and return empty list (but still mark tool available for PoC simplicity). For robustness, also check `result.returncode` against known failure codes (e.g., pyright returns 0 on success, 1 on type errors, 2 on fatal error). The simplest sufficient fix: in each runner, after checking for `"NOT_FOUND"`, add:
if result.stderr and not result.stderr.startswith(("NOT_FOUND", "TIMEOUT")):
    logger.error("%s reported error: %s", tool_name, result.stderr[:200])
This at least surfaces the failure without changing the interface.

all_findings.description:
FIND — the “health scan” omits CrossHair entirely even though the module-level contract and tool list explicitly advertise it as part of the endocrine layer (`CROSSHAIR_BIN`, `_CROSSHAIR_TIMEOUT`, tool docstring says crosshair exists alongside pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy). There is no `run_crosshair()` implementation and `scan_health()` never invokes it.
FOLLOW: This is not just unused constants; it means one advertised health-scan capability never fires. Reviewers and downstream logic may believe symbolic analysis is part of the inter-round scan when it is absent. The discrepancy also biases fix evaluation and health totals because only syntax/type/lint/security tools contribute. In PoC terms, a claimed feature is dead and reviewer-facing outputs overstate what was checked.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — remove CrossHair from the endocrine interface and binary declarations for now so the reported capabilities match reality.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The endocrine layer’s pacing signal for “novelty plateau” uses `novelty_counts` list without specifying how it is populated. The insect brain must provide this list, but the interface documentation does not define its semantics (counts per round, cumulative, etc.). Evidence: `compute_pacing_signals` signature `novelty_counts: List[int]` and the comment “List of novel finding counts per round (index = round)”. However, the function assumes `novelty_counts` is indexed by round and contains counts for each round up to `round_idx`. If the insect brain provides a list of only non‑zero counts, the indexing breaks.
FOLLOW: Downstream: The novelty plateau signal may fire incorrectly (too early or never), causing the insect brain to misjudge convergence. This could lead to premature termination or unnecessary rounds.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Clarify in the docstring that `novelty_counts` must be a list where `novelty_counts[i]` is the novel finding count for round `i`. If the list is shorter than `round_idx`, pad with zeros. For the PoC, assume the insect brain passes correct data (as it does in the current implementation). No code change required.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` slow‑model detection uses `median_duration * 2.5` as threshold, but if one model is extremely slow, it can skew the median upward, preventing detection of other slow models. Evidence: lines 455-461. The median is calculated from all durations, then each model is compared to `median_duration * 2.5`. If one model takes 300s and others take 5s, median may be 5s, threshold 12.5s, and the 300s model is detected. However, if two models are slow (e.g., 300s and 200s), median could be 200s, threshold 500s, and neither is detected.
FOLLOW: Downstream: Slow models may go undetected, causing rounds to stall without the insect brain taking corrective action (e.g., increase timeout). This can lead to budget exhaustion without convergence.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Use a fixed threshold (e.g., 30s) combined with a relative threshold (e.g., > 2× the minimum duration). For PoC, the current logic is acceptable because extreme skew is unlikely with 5 models. No fix needed.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `run_bandit()` invokes `bandit` without recursive/file-target disambiguation, but `scan_health()` passes a list of source files. Bandit CLI commonly expects `-r` for directories and can behave inconsistently for multiple file operands depending on version/wrapper; endocrine assumes JSON `results` will always correspond directly to the requested paths and does no return-code validation. Evidence: `cmd = [BANDIT_BIN, "-f", "json", "-q"] + paths`; unlike ruff/pyright, there is no explicit mode selection or handling for execution failure beyond `NOT_FOUND`.
FOLLOW: Health scans can silently miss security diagnostics or treat execution failures as clean runs, degrading the core “health scan correctly run tools and parse output” feature. Because counts feed the insect brain as structured health signals, reviewers can be shown an artificially healthy security state.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — invoke bandit in explicit file mode per file (looping over paths and aggregating JSON results) so execution semantics are stable and failures can be attributed per file.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()`’s documented/typed contract is `context_budget: int`, but the implementation branches on `isinstance(context_budget, dict)`. The annotation and `EndocrineLayer.run()` signature remain `int`, so dict callers are relying on an undocumented interface. Existing registry covers non-numeric crash risk, but there is a separate interface bug: the function’s accepted input domain and public signature disagree.
FOLLOW: This crosses the endocrine→brain boundary because callers cannot know whether per-model budget maps are supported, and static analysis/type-checking of this integration will flag or discourage the very input shape the function handles at runtime. In PoC terms, that creates avoidable integration drift and hidden behavior around pacing thresholds.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — change the public type signature of `compute_pacing_signals()` and `EndocrineLayer.run()` to accept `int | dict[str, int]`, and document the reduction rule used.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_find_target_file` uses a brittle regex to extract file paths from the finding description. The regex `[\w/\\]+\.py\b` matches sequences of word chars, slashes, and backslashes ending with `.py`. It fails on paths with hyphens, dots, or spaces; it also matches substrings like `import.py` inside text. Evidence: lines 476‑477. The fallback to `source_paths[0]` is arbitrary and likely wrong when multiple source files exist.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequence: fix evaluation may be applied to the wrong source file, producing incorrect verdicts (SAFE/HARMFUL). If the wrong file is patched, the before/after tool counts are meaningless. The endocrine layer may mark a finding as verified based on an unrelated file, causing the bug‑closed gate to incorrectly close a bug. This is a silent wrong result.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Use the file‑path extraction already implemented in the immune pipeline’s skin barrier (see `immune_agents.py`, function `skin_barrier_check`). That function uses a more robust pattern `(\S+\.\w+)(?::|\s+line\s+)(\d+)` and matches against known source paths. Reuse that logic, or at least check that the extracted path exists in `source_paths` (or is a suffix of one). If no match, return `None` and mark fix UNEVALUABLE with a clear error.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` novelty plateau detection uses `novelty_counts` list where index = round. However, the endocrine layer receives `novelty_counts` from the insect brain, which may be a list of novel finding counts per round, but the indices may not align if the experiment started at round 0. The check `if len(novelty_counts) >= 3 and round_idx >= 2:` then uses `novelty_counts[-3:]` which assumes the list contains counts for rounds up to `round_idx`. If the list is shorter (e.g., novelty counts only for rounds where novel findings >0), the window is misaligned. Evidence: lines 494‑500.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequence: novelty plateau signal may fire incorrectly (too early or too late), causing the insect brain to incorrectly signal convergence. This could terminate the experiment prematurely or let it run past convergence.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Assume `novelty_counts` length equals `round_idx + 1` (one entry per round, including zero counts). Document this requirement. Add a defensive clamp: `window = novelty_counts[max(0, round_idx-2):round_idx+1]` and check `len(window) == 3`. If not, skip the signal.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health` runs all four static analysis tools sequentially on every source file between every round. For a medium‑sized codebase (10‑20 files), this may take 10‑30 seconds per round, adding up over many rounds. The endocrine layer is meant to run between rounds; if rounds are short (e.g., 2‑3 minutes), the health scan becomes a significant overhead. Evidence: lines 250‑270, loop over tools calling `runner(existing)`.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequence: experiment duration increases, risking context budget exhaustion before convergence. This is a performance issue, not correctness, but for PoC it may be acceptable. However, if the scan exceeds the inter‑round timeout, the endocrine layer may crash or produce incomplete reports.
all_findings.proposed_fix: For PoC, keep sequential execution but add a timeout to the entire `scan_health` function (e.g., 30 seconds). If timeout is reached, return a partial HealthScan with diagnostics collected so far and log a warning. This ensures the endocrine layer does not hang.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The `DefectCategory` class is not an enum but used as string tags. This allows typos and inconsistent category strings across the codebase. Evidence: lines 62‑71, categories defined as class attributes. Used in `_categorise_pyright`, `_categorise_ruff`, etc. A typo (e.g., `TYPE_SAFETY` vs `TYPE_SAFETY`) would cause silent miscounts.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequence: aggregate counts by category may be wrong because of string mismatches, leading to incorrect health trends. The insect brain’s decisions based on these trends may be suboptimal.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Convert `DefectCategory` to an `Enum` and use `Enum.value` for string representation. Update all categorisation functions to return `DefectCategory` members. This ensures type safety and prevents typos.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `scan_health()` omits unavailable tools from `tools_available` entirely when `source_paths` is empty or when a runner returns `[]` on launcher failure, producing an ambiguous report shape. The report consumer cannot distinguish “tool absent”, “tool present and found zero diagnostics”, and “no scan run.” Evidence: empty-input path returns `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` with default empty `tools_available`; normal path only sets keys inside the loop and relies on runner success rather than actual execution status.
FOLLOW: The insect brain receives an under-specified health report. Missing keys force consumers to infer state from absence, while other cases use explicit booleans. This weakens interface correctness and compounds C0001/C0004: the endocrine layer can both overstate health and omit state entirely depending on path. Downstream dashboards or logic comparing tool readiness across rounds can misread disappearing keys as schema drift or healthy zero-findings scans.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — always populate `tools_available` for every configured tool with explicit booleans, including the no-source-path early return, and derive those booleans from actual tool execution status rather than empty diagnostic lists.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong source file by substring match. Evidence: it returns a path if `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. The `match in sp_path` branch is overly loose: a mention like `brain.py` can match `insect_brain.py`; directory fragments can also collide across unrelated paths. The function then falls back to the first source path if no precise match exists.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can patch and analyze the wrong file while still producing a concrete verdict.
