Because the result is keyed only by `finding_id`, downstream consumers will believe the proposed fix was evaluated for the intended bug. This can produce both false SAFE and false HARMFUL classifications and undermine verified-fix propagation.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — remove the generic substring match and resolve only by exact normalized path match, basename match, or suffix path-component match; if resolution is ambiguous, return `None` and mark the fix `UNEVALUABLE` instead of guessing.

all_findings.description:
FIND — In `compute_pacing_signals`, the slow‑model detection uses a hard‑coded threshold of 30 seconds (`rt.duration_s > 30.0`). For a PoC with fast rounds, this may never trigger, even if a model is significantly slower than others.
FOLLOW: The insect brain will not receive a “slow_model” pacing signal, potentially causing timeout‑related failures in later rounds if a model consistently exceeds the median but stays under 30 seconds.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Make the absolute threshold configurable (e.g., via `EndocrineLayer` constructor) or derive it dynamically as a multiple of the median (e.g., `median_duration * 2.5` and `rt.duration_s > 10.0`). For PoC, lower the threshold to 10 seconds.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The `ToolDiagnostic` dataclass uses `severity` as a string, but the values are tool‑specific (“error”, “warning”, “info” for pyright; “warning” for ruff; mapped strings for bandit). This inconsistent representation makes aggregate severity counts (`counts_by_severity`) misleading.
FOLLOW: The health scan’s severity aggregation mixes different tool‑specific severity levels, reducing the utility of the `counts_by_severity` metric for the insect brain.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Normalize severity across tools to a common scale (e.g., “ERROR”, “WARNING”, “INFO”) using a mapping per tool. For ruff, map “warning” → “WARNING”. For pyright, map “error” → “ERROR”, “warning” → “WARNING”, “info” → “INFO”. For bandit, map “HIGH” → “ERROR”, “MEDIUM” → “WARNING”, “LOW” → “INFO”.

all_findings.description:
FIND — In `scan_health`, the `tools_available` dict is populated by catching exceptions from each runner. However, the runner functions (`run_pyright`, etc.) catch exceptions internally and return empty lists, so they rarely raise. Thus `tools_available` may be `True` even if the tool binary is missing (because the runner returns `[]` without raising).
FOLLOW: The health scan will incorrectly report that a tool is available when it is not, leading the insect brain to believe static analysis coverage is complete when it is not.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Modify each runner to return a tuple `(diagnostics, tool_found: bool)`. The `tool_found` flag should be `False` if `_run_tool` returns `stderr="NOT_FOUND"` or `stderr="TIMEOUT"`. Then `scan_health` can set `tools_available` based on that flag.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The `DefectCategory` class includes `STYLE` and `UNKNOWN`, but the categorisation functions (`_categorise_pyright`, `_categorise_ruff`) never return `UNKNOWN`. All pyright diagnostics are categorised as `TYPE_SAFETY` or `NULL_DEREF`; all ruff diagnostics as `DEAD_CODE`, `STYLE`, or `SECURITY`. Unknown patterns are forced into these categories.
FOLLOW: The defect detection feature misrepresents the nature of some diagnostics, reducing the accuracy of the `counts_by_category` signal for the insect brain.
all_findings.proposed_fix: In each categorisation function, add a fall‑back that returns `DefectCategory.UNKNOWN` when no known pattern matches. This preserves the semantic distinction between “known category” and “unknown”.

all_findings.description:
FIND — The `EndocrineLayer` stores a history of `HealthScan` objects (`_scan_history`) but never limits its size. Over many rounds, this list grows unbounded, consuming memory.
FOLLOW: In a long‑running experiment, the endocrine layer’s memory footprint grows without bound, potentially leading to out‑of‑memory errors.
all_findings.proposed_fix: Limit `_scan_history` to the last N scans (e.g., 50) or discard old scans after a certain number of rounds. For PoC, this is low priority, but the fix is trivial: in `run`, after appending, `self._scan_history = self._scan_history[-50:]`.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `_count_tool_issues` catches all `Exception`s and returns `0` when a static analysis tool runner crashes.
FOLLOW: If a proposed fix severely corrupts the syntax of a file, causing a tool runner (e.g., Pyright or Ruff) to crash or raise an unhandled exception during `evaluate_fix`, it records `new_errors = 0`. If the original file had pre-existing errors, the net change becomes negative. `_compute_fix_verdict` evaluates this as successfully resolving all issues, marking the completely broken file as `SAFE` and pushing it through the verification gate.

FIND — the health scan advertises “pyright/ruff/bandit” static analysis between rounds, but `scan_health()` also runs `mypy` unconditionally and exposes its diagnostics in totals. This creates an interface mismatch with the documented endocrine contract and with downstream interpretation of health metrics. Evidence: module header and “The endocrine layer provides” list mention pyright/ruff/bandit; `scan_health()` iterates over `("pyright", "ruff", "bandit", "mypy")`.
FOLLOW: This is not just documentation drift. Health totals, counts_by_tool, counts_by_severity, and counts_by_category are inflated by an extra checker that the rest of the system is not told to expect. Pacing or human review based on “health scan” can interpret increased errors as regressions from the promised three-tool baseline. The same inconsistency affects fix evaluation, where pre/post type counts use pyright only, while health scan type counts include both pyright and mypy; the two endocrine outputs become incomparable.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — make the contract consistent by either removing mypy from `scan_health()` for the PoC, or updating the public endocrine interface/docstrings to explicitly state that mypy is part of the health scan and fix-evaluation metrics. The simpler sufficient fix is to remove mypy from `scan_health()` until it is an intentional surfaced feature.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `health_trend()` is structurally incompatible with its own contract “diagnostic count trends across rounds (by category)” because it only appends counts for categories present in each scan: `for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. Registry findings C0002/C0006 already cover omitted zero-count rounds for categories that disappear. This method has a second, separate interface bug: categories that appear for the first time in later rounds get shorter histories starting mid-series, so the returned lists are not aligned to round indices at all. Example: if category A first appears in round 3, `trend["A"] == [count_round_3]`, which the caller cannot map onto full round history without extra reconstruction.
FOLLOW: Any consumer treating index `i` as round `i` gets wrong trends, even if it handles “missing zero” for existing categories. This can mislead any future trend-based pacing or health regression logic in the insect brain by shifting late-appearing categories earlier in time. Because the method advertises round trends, this is a silent interface error, not mere formatting.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — build trends over the full union of categories across all scans and emit one entry per scan in round order for every category, using `0` when absent. That simultaneously fixes missing-zero and late-category misalignment.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `compute_pacing_signals` novelty plateau detection uses the wrong list index. It checks `if len(novelty_counts) >= 3 and round_idx >= 2: recent = novelty_counts[-3:]`. However, `novelty_counts` is a list of counts per round, indexed by round number. At `round_idx=2`, the list has indices 0,1,2. Taking `[-3:]` yields all three elements, but the condition `all(n <= 1 for n in recent)` will be evaluating rounds 0,1,2 — i.e., the first three rounds of the experiment. That’s too early to declare a novelty plateau. The intention is to look at the last three rounds, but at round 2 there are only three total rounds. This will fire a false positive early in the experiment. Evidence: lines 487–495 in endocrine.py.

FOLLOW:  
1. False pacing signal: The insect brain may receive a “novelty_plateau” signal in round 2, causing it to check convergence prematurely and potentially terminate the experiment early.  
2. Early termination: If the experiment stops at round 2 because of a false plateau, critical bugs may be missed.  
3. Wasted PoC: The proof‑of‑concept fails to reach enough rounds to demonstrate end‑to‑end operation.

FIND — the advertised “defect detection” categories do not actually include dead-code detection from type checkers/linters beyond coarse pyright/ruff heuristics, and `scan_health()` never invokes any classifier over the aggregated diagnostics despite the module contract claiming a separate capability “Defect detection — classify findings by defect category”. In implementation there is no standalone defect-detection function; categorisation only happens incidentally inside individual runners.
FOLLOW: This feature boundary matters to `insect_brain`, which receives a `HealthScan` as if the endocrine layer has performed a complete classification stage. Missing categories and the absence of a dedicated pass mean some promised signals never fire, reducing the usefulness of health data for pacing/decision logic and misleading human reviewers about what the endocrine layer actually checked.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — make the contract honest for the PoC: remove the standalone “Defect detection” capability claim from the module/class docstrings and describe categorisation as best-effort tagging attached to tool diagnostics.

all_findings.description:
FIND — `health_trend()` drops categories that were absent in early rounds, so the returned series are not aligned to absolute round numbers. The method appends counts only when a category appears in a scan: `trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. If a category first appears in round 3, its list starts at length 1 rather than `[0,0,1,...]`.
FOLLOW: Downstream consumers cannot distinguish “category absent in prior rounds” from “history starts later”, so trend deltas are shifted left for late-appearing categories. Any insect-brain or human review logic using these lists for worsening/improving health will compute the wrong temporal location of regressions. This is a separate correctness issue from the existing ragged-series findings because it specifically breaks round alignment, not just zero omission within existing categories.
all_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — emit one entry per recorded scan for every category by building the union of categories across `_scan_history` and filling missing rounds with zero before returning.

finding.description:
FIND — scan_health() misreports missing tools as available. In bench/endocrine.py, each runner returns `[]` when `_run_tool()` reports `stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`, and scan_health() then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` unconditionally unless an exception was raised. Evidence: run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy all convert NOT_FOUND into empty diagnostics instead of surfacing unavailability, and scan_health has no other availability check.
FOLLOW: This creates a fail-open health scan: the endocrine layer can report a clean scan with zero diagnostics while all analyzers are absent. insect_brain consumes health_scan as a structured health signal for round decisions; zero diagnostics from “available” tools is materially different from “tool unavailable”. It also corrupts reviewer-facing telemetry and can hide infrastructure regressions in the PoC happy path, since the whole health monitor appears to function while doing nothing.
finding.proposed_fix: FIX — propagate tool availability explicitly from each runner or from _run_tool returncode/stderr, and in scan_health mark a tool unavailable when invocation returned NOT_FOUND or TIMEOUT instead of treating empty diagnostics as success.

triaged.extracted_claim: stderr == "NOT_FOUND", tools_available[tool_name] = True

finding.description:
FIND — health_trend() produces ragged time series that omit zero-count rounds for categories absent in a scan. It appends counts only for categories present in each scan’s `counts_by_category`; categories missing in a round get no entry. After scans like `{security: 1}` then `{style: 1}`, the returned trend is `{"security": [1], "style": [1]}` instead of aligned per-round series like `{"security": [1,0], "style": [0,1]}`.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing category trends across rounds receives malformed history and can misread disappearance as missing data rather than zero. Since this method exists specifically “for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health,” ragged vectors make trend analysis and thresholding unreliable.
finding.proposed_fix: FIX — build the union of categories across scan history and emit one count per round per category, inserting 0 when a category is absent in a given scan.

triaged.extracted_claim:
FIND — health_trend() produces ragged time series that omit zero-count rounds for categories absent in a scan. It appends counts only for categories present in each scan’s `counts_by_category`; categories missing in a round get no entry. After scans like `{security: 1}` then `{style: 1}`, the returned trend is `{"security": [1], "style": [1]}` instead of aligned per-round series like `{"security": [1,0], "style": [0,1]}`.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing category trends across rounds receives malformed history and can misread disappearance as missing data rather than zero. Since this method exists specifically “for the insect brain to detect worsening/improving code health,” ragged vectors make trend analysis and thresholding unreliable.

finding.description:
FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is partially dead code. endocrine.py declares DefectCategory.OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION, and the module docstring claims defect classification for “off-by-one” and “race conditions,” but no categoriser path in run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy ever emits either category. All pyright/mypy diagnostics collapse to TYPE_SAFETY or NULL_DEREF; ruff mostly maps to DEAD_CODE/STYLE/SECURITY.
FOLLOW: Downstream, counts_by_category and any reviewer relying on endocrine defect categories will never see those categories fire, so the feature does not deliver the claimed coverage. In a PoC this is medium severity rather than critical, but it is still misleading telemetry and effectively dead functionality.
finding.proposed_fix: FIX — either add minimal pattern-based mappings that can actually emit OFF_BY_ONE and RACE_CONDITION from tool messages, or remove those categories from the advertised capability until supported. The simpler sufficient fix is to stop advertising unsupported categories.

All pyright/mypy diagnostics collapse to TYPE_SAFETY or NULL_DEREF; ruff mostly maps to DEAD_CODE/STYLE/SECURITY.
FOLLOW: Downstream, counts_by_category and any reviewer relying on endocrine defect categories will never see those categories fire, so the feature does not deliver the claimed coverage. finding.description:
FIND — Tool runners (`run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, `run_bandit`, `run_mypy`) silently swallow tool execution failures, returning empty diagnostics while marking tools as available. When a tool exits with a non-zero code due to an internal error (e.g., syntax error in source, missing module, out-of-memory), the runner logs a JSON parse warning but still returns an empty list. The `scan_health` function then incorrectly marks the tool as `True` in `tools_available`. Evidence: In `run_pyright`, if `json.loads(result.stdout)` fails (JSONDecodeError), the function logs a warning and returns `[]`. No check of `result.stderr` for error messages. Same pattern in `run_ruff`, `run_bandit`, and `run_mypy`.
FOLLOW: This leads to incorrect health metrics: missing diagnostics, inflated tool availability, and misleading health signals to the insect brain. Downstream, `evaluate_fix` uses `_count_tool_issues` which calls these same runners; if a tool fails silently, the fix evaluation will see 0 issues pre- and post-fix, leading to incorrect `NEUTRAL` or `SAFE` verdicts. The insect brain may incorrectly conclude code health is improving when tools are actually failing.
finding.proposed_fix:
Add explicit error detection in each runner: after the `"NOT_FOUND"` and `"TIMEOUT"` checks, examine `result.stderr` for indications of tool failure (non-empty stderr that isn't a known warning pattern). If present, log an error and return empty list (but still mark tool available for PoC simplicity). For robustness, also check `result.returncode` against known failure codes (e.g., pyright returns 0 on success, 1 on type errors, 2 on fatal error). The simplest sufficient fix: in each runner, after checking for `"NOT_FOUND"`, add:
if result.stderr and not result.stderr.startswith(("NOT_FOUND", "TIMEOUT")):
    logger.error("%s reported error: %s", tool_name, result.stderr[:200])
This at least surfaces the failure without changing the interface.

However, `novelty_counts` is a list of counts per round, indexed by round number. At `round_idx=2`, the list has indices 0,1,2. Taking `[-3:]` yields all three elements, but the condition `all(n <= 1 for n in recent)` will be evaluating rounds 0,1,2 — i.e., the first three rounds of the experiment. That’s too early to declare a novelty plateau. The intention is to look at the last three rounds, but at round 2 there are only three total rounds. This will fire a false positive early in the experiment. Evidence: lines 487–495 in endocrine.py.

FOLLOW:  
1. False pacing signal: The insect brain may receive a “novelty_plateau” signal in round 2, causing it to check convergence prematurely and potentially terminate the experiment early.  
2. Early termination: If the experiment stops at round 2 because of a false plateau, critical bugs may be missed.  
3. Wasted PoC: The proof‑of‑concept fails to reach enough rounds to demonstrate end‑to‑end operation.

filtered_findings.description:
FIND — the health scan advertises “pyright/ruff/bandit” static analysis between rounds, but `scan_health()` also runs `mypy` unconditionally and exposes its diagnostics in totals. This creates an interface mismatch with the documented endocrine contract and with downstream interpretation of health metrics. Evidence: module header and “The endocrine layer provides” list mention pyright/ruff/bandit; `scan_health()` iterates over `("pyright", "ruff", "bandit", "mypy")`.
FOLLOW: This is not just documentation drift. Health totals, counts_by_tool, counts_by_severity, and counts_by_category are inflated by an extra checker that the rest of the system is not told to expect. Pacing or human review based on “health scan” can interpret increased errors as regressions from the promised three-tool baseline. The same inconsistency affects fix evaluation, where pre/post type counts use pyright only, while health scan type counts include both pyright and mypy; the two endocrine outputs become incomparable.
filtered_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — make the contract consistent by either removing mypy from `scan_health()` for the PoC, or updating the public endocrine interface/docstrings to explicitly state that mypy is part of the health scan and fix-evaluation metrics. The simpler sufficient fix is to remove mypy from `scan_health()` until it is an intentional surfaced feature.

rejected_findings.description:
FIND — `health_trend()` is structurally incompatible with its own contract “diagnostic count trends across rounds (by category)” because it only appends counts for categories present in each scan: `for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. Registry findings C0002/C0006 already cover omitted zero-count rounds for categories that disappear. This method has a second, separate interface bug: categories that appear for the first time in later rounds get shorter histories starting mid-series, so the returned lists are not aligned to round indices at all. Example: if category A first appears in round 3, `trend["A"] == [count_round_3]`, which the caller cannot map onto full round history without extra reconstruction.
FOLLOW: Any consumer treating index `i` as round `i` gets wrong trends, even if it handles “missing zero” for existing categories. This can mislead any future trend-based pacing or health regression logic in the insect brain by shifting late-appearing categories earlier in time. Because the method advertises round trends, this is a silent interface error, not mere formatting.
rejected_findings.proposed_fix: FIX — build trends over the full union of categories across all scans and emit one entry per scan in round order for every category, using `0` when absent. That simultaneously fixes missing-zero and late-category misalignment.
